Consider that mathematical research pre-Python was done manually in notebooks, libraries assembled from scratch.

This is my attempt at forecasting.
For context, you might ask how I earned my special skill. Stick with me, this will be useful later.
I participated in a competition to achieve the goal"AIs solve all open Millenium Prize Problems" using only one neurosymbolic agent.

Given that I watched the competition, I've since taught myself the 1997 algorithm that almost won it.

Today's prompt does not apply to my knowledge at that time. Too bad. This agent (MAD) earned that 2% multiplicative probability by counting accomplishments. This system attempted to solve math problems located at different depths within a reified tree, where problems served as leaves. The most straightforward problems, called "Primitives," where coefficients and constants crossed a Critical Threshold always returned 0% or 100%. MAD tried to calculate higher-scoring leaves by searching their subtrees to find Primitives. Higher scoring nodes contained higher-scoring Primitives, and subtrees were repeatedly used to solve simpler problems. Many problems remained unsolved at the 1997 level of mathematics as humans were at work on many of them. 5 and 6 were just the Depth the I could solve then. I could not predict their solution date.
formatted_prompt:
Forecast date: 2024-09-19. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Assign a probability to the event occurring on or before each of the listed deadlines. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.
